arxiv-1804-10396.creator: Louisa Seelbach Benkner, Markus Lohrey and Stephan Wagner
arxiv-1804-10396.description: Abstract . We study the average number of distinct fringe subtrees in random trees generated by leaf-centric binary tree sources as introduced by Zhang, Yang and Kieffer in [ 32 ] . A leaf-centric binary tree source induces for every n ≥ 2 n\geq 2 a probability distribution on the set of binary trees with n n leaves.

arxiv-2005-03886.title: A non-commutative Bayes’ theorem
arxiv-2005-03886.creator: Arthur J. Parzygnat, Benjamin P. Russo
arxiv-2005-03886.description: Abstract Using a diagrammatic reformulation of Bayes’ theorem, we provide a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of Bayesian inference in the setting of finite-dimensional C ∗ C^{*} -algebras. In other words, we prove an analogue of Bayes’ theorem in the joint classical and quantum context.

arxiv-2012-07697.title: Nonlinear state-space identification using deep encoder networks
arxiv-2012-07697.creator: Gerben Beintema, Roland Toth, Maarten Schoukens
arxiv-2012-07697.description: Abstract Nonlinear state-space identification for dynamical systems is most often performed by minimizing the simulation error to reduce the effect of model errors. This optimization problem becomes computationally expensive for large datasets. Moreover, the problem is also strongly non-convex, often leading to sub-optimal parameter estimates.

arxiv-2101-06088.title: Exploring the sensitivity of hadron colliders to non-universality in heavy neutral currents
arxiv-2101-06088.creator: F. A. Conventi 1,2, G. D’Ambrosio 1, A.M. Iyer 3, E. Rossi 1,4
arxiv-2101-06088.description: Abstract We present sensitivity projections for discovering a heavy resonance decaying to electron and muon pairs and for probing the charged lepton non-universality in such decays at the HL-LHC and FCC-hh. The analysis takes into account the expected differences in the reconstruction efficiencies and the dilepton mass resolutions for dielectron and dimuon final states.

arxiv-2306-13119.title: Adversarial Resilience in Sequential Prediction via Abstention Thanks: A part of this work was done while S. Goel was a postdoctoral researcher at Microsoft Research NYC. Thanks: A part of this work was done while A. Shetty was an intern at Microsoft Research NYC.
arxiv-2306-13119.description: Abstract We study the problem of sequential prediction in the stochastic setting with an adversary that is allowed to inject clean-label adversarial (or out-of-distribution) examples. Algorithms designed to handle purely stochastic data tend to fail in the presence of such adversarial examples, often leading to erroneous predictions.

arxiv-2306-14910.title: The Importance of Human-Labeled Data in the Era of LLMs
arxiv-2306-14910.creator: Yang Liu
arxiv-2306-14910.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yang Liu. The advent of large language models (LLMs) has brought about a revolution in the development of tailored machine learning models and sparked debates on redefining data requirements. The automation facilitated by the training and implementation of LLMs has led to discussions and aspirations that human-level labeling interventions may no longer hold the same level of importance as in the era of supervised learning. This paper presents compelling arguments supporting the ongoing relevance of human-labeled data in the era of LLMs.

arxiv-2312-15158.title: Map-Reduce for Multiprocessing Large Data and Multi-threading for Data Scraping
arxiv-2312-15158.creator: Zefeng Qiu 1 , Prashanth Umapathy 2 , Qingquan Zhang 3 , Guanqun Song 4 , Ting Zhu 5
arxiv-2312-15158.description: Abstract This document is the final project report for our advanced operating system class. During this project, we mainly focused on applying multiprocessing and multi-threading technology to our whole project and utilized the map-reduce algorithm in our data cleaning and data analysis process.

arxiv-2401-14345.title: Uncovering Heterogeneity of Solar Flare Mechanism With Mixture Models
arxiv-2401-14345.creator: Bach Viet Do, Yang Chen, XuanLong Nguyen, Ward Manchester
arxiv-2401-14345.description: Abstract The physics of solar flares occurring on the Sun is highly complex and far from fully understood. However, observations show that solar eruptions are associated with the intense kilogauss fields of active regions, where free energies are stored with field-aligned electric currents.

arxiv-2504-07477.title: Analog Computing for Signal Processing and Communications – Part II: Toward Gigantic MIMO Beamforming
arxiv-2504-07477.creator: Matteo Nerini, Bruno Clerckx
arxiv-2504-07477.description: Abstract Analog-domain operations offer a promising solution to accelerating signal processing and enabling future multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications with thousands of antennas. In Part I of this paper, we have introduced a microwave linear analog computer (MiLAC) as an analog computer that processes microwave signals linearly, demonstrating its potential to reduce the computational complexity of specific signal processing tasks.

arxiv-2506-01550.title: Alignment Phase Transition in Socially Driven Motion
arxiv-2506-01550.creator: Debasish Sarker, Yi Zhang, Lynn K. Perry, Daniel S. Messinger, Chaoming Song
arxiv-2506-01550.description: Abstract Collective human movement is a hallmark of complex systems, exhibiting emergent order across diverse settings, from pedestrian flows to biological collectives. In high-speed scenarios, alignment interactions ensure efficient flow and navigation. In contrast, alignment in low-speed, socially engaged contexts emerges not from locomotion goals but from interpersonal interaction.

arxiv-2509-03818.title: A Versatile and Programmable UAV Platform for Radio Access Network and End-to-End Cellular Measurements
arxiv-2509-03818.creator: Sherwan Jalal Abdullah 1 , Sravan Reddy Chintareddy 1 , Victor S. Frost 1 , Shawn Keshmiri 2 , Morteza Hashemi 1
arxiv-2509-03818.description: Abstract In this work, we develop a measurement platform to capture mobile network performance metrics including coverage and quality of service in regions where conventional coverage testing approaches are frequently time-intensive, labor-demanding, and occasionally hazardous. Traditionally, crowd-sourcing methods are used to collect cellular network performance metrics.

arxiv-2509-18946.title: Soret and Dufour effects in hot and dense QCD matter
arxiv-2509-18946.creator: Kamaljeet Singh, Kangkan Goswami, Raghunath Sahoo
arxiv-2509-18946.description: Abstract The gradients act as invisible engines of transport, converting microscopic imbalances into macroscopic flows, and thus providing deep insights into the dynamics of physical systems. Thermal gradients do not merely drive the flow of heat, but they also set the microscopic constituents of the system into motion.

Ectopic expression of many members of this network leads to the transformation of non-retinal epithelia int

pmc-10743161.title: Thermoreversible Gel-Dispersed Liquid Crystals
pmc-10743161.creator: Akihiko Matsuyama
pmc-10743161.description: A simple model is introduced to describe phase behaviours of binary mixtures of a thermoreversible gel and a low-molecular-weight liquid crystal (LC). We predict novel phase diagrams on the temperature–concentration plane, including sol–gel transition, nematic–isotropic phase transition, and phase separation. At high temperatures, the phase separation between the isotropic sol and gel phases appears.

pmc-11287725.title: Congenital hydrocephalus and ligneous conjunctivitis in two children with severe type I plasminogen deficiency: A case report and literature review
pmc-11287725.creator: Doha Jaber, Inas Jaber, Tumodir Abdallah, Hadi Dababseh, Abdalwahab Kharousha
pmc-11287725.description: Type I plasminogen (PLG I) deficiency is a genetic disorder inherited in an autosomal recessive mode and carries high mortality and morbidity. This case report discusses two babies, aged 2 and 3 months, who were diagnosed with ligneous conjunctivitis and congenital hydrocephalus. They had progressive macrocephaly, which led to the insertion of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt.

pmc-11420478.title: Integrated bioinformatics analysis and validation identify KIR2DL4 as a novel biomarker for predicting chemotherapy resistance and prognosis in colorectal cancer
pmc-11420478.creator: HuiE. Zhuang, Yizhen Chen
pmc-11420478.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundChemotherapy and immunotherapy have improved the cure rate and survival period for colorectal cancer (CRC), but genetic heterogeneity among patients leads to chemotherapy resistance and disease progression. Identifying new molecular markers is crucial for improving prognosis for CRC patients. KIR2DL4, a transmembrane glycoprotein expressed by immune cells, has shown potential therapeutic and prognostic value in other cancers, but in CRC remains unclear.MethodsThis study validated the expression levels of KIR2DL4 in CRC by integrating multiple public databases and assessed through immunohistochemistry (IHC).

pmc-11545014.title: Commentary: A Comparison of the Methods of the Pre-Slaughter Stunning of Cattle in Australia—Mechanical, Electrical, and Diathermic Syncope
pmc-11545014.creator: Gabrielle C Musk, Craig B Johnson, Temple Grandin
pmc-11545014.description: Simple SummaryCattle in Australian abattoirs are slaughtered using a two-step method. The first step causes loss of consciousness by stunning, while the second step causes death from blood loss. The methods for causing unconsciousness include applying electrical current to the brain, applying mechanical force to the brain, or a new system of heating the brain tissue selectively (diathermic syncope).

pmc-11710160.title: Meningeal and infiltrating T‐cells are associated with neuroinflammation after head injury and with tau pathology in CTE
pmc-11710160.creator: Samantha M Calderazzo, Thor D. Stein, David M. Holtzman, Ann C. McKee, Bertrand Russell Huber
pmc-11710160.description: BackgroundT‐cell infiltration into the brain parenchyma is associated with hyperphosphorylated tau (p‐tau) accumulation in neurodegenerative diseases. Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a progressive tauopathy caused by exposure to repetitive head impacts (RHI). CTE is defined by the perivascular accumulation of p‐tau at the cortical sulcal depths and can be stratified into mild and severe pathological stages.

pmc-12425481.title: Cellular characterization of the mouse collecting lymphatic vessels reveals that lymphatic muscle cells are the innate pacemaker cells
pmc-12425481.creator: Scott D Zawieja, Grace A Pea, Sarah E Broyhill, Advaya Patro, Karen H Bromert, Charles E Norton, Hae Jin Kim, Sathesh Kumar Sivasankaran, Min Li, Jorge A Castorena-Gonzalez, Bernard T Drumm, Michael J Davis, Mark T Nelson, Scott D Zawieja, Grace A Pea, Sarah E Broyhill, Advaya Patro, Karen H Bromert
pmc-12425481.description: Collecting lymphatic vessels (cLVs) exhibit spontaneous contractions with a pressure-dependent frequency, but the identity of the lymphatic pacemaker cell is still debated. Here, we combined immunofluorescence and scRNAseq analyses with electrophysiological methods to examine the cellular constituents of the mouse cLV wall and assess whether any cell type exhibited morphological and functional processes characteristic of pacemaker cells.

pmc-12562528.title: Characteristics and Distribution of Radiologists in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study Based on National Data
pmc-12562528.creator: Jaber Hussain Alsalah, Daniele Giansanti
pmc-12562528.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: In healthcare institutions, radiologists play an essential role in patients’ care, enabling them to begin treatment and start their recoveries. However, data on the characteristics and distribution of the radiology workforce in Saudi Arabia are limited. Therefore, this study aimed to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the radiology workforce in SA based on national data and identify key distributional and specialty trends relevant to workforce planning and radiology service delivery.

pmc-12648767.title: Ruthenium Bis-Sulfonate Complexes: Synthesis and Application in Asymmetric Hydrogenation
pmc-12648767.creator: Yifei Zhou, Pim Vink, Ibrahim Kılınç, Olga O. Sokolova, Fedor M. Miloserdov
pmc-12648767.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). A series of Ru­(L)­(X)2 complexes (L = bidentate ligand; X = OMs, OTs, OTf) was synthesized and characterized. Ru­(BINAP)­(OMs)2 showed improved catalytic performance over the established Ru­(BINAP)­(OAc)2 catalyst, highlighting the impact of anion variation on catalytic asymmetric hydrogenations. Asymmetric hydrogenation (AH) is a prominent and versatile catalytic transformation for the selective and efficient reduction of double bonds (CO, CN, CC) with near-perfect atom economy.

pmc-13412150.title: Sustainable Mite Management in Apple Orchards Under Climatic Stress: Ecological Trade-Offs and System Challenges
pmc-13412150.creator: Assel A. Karabayeva, Bakyt K. Kopzhassarov, Gulzhan B. Sarseyeva, Gulnar K. Ziyayeva, Assem D. Nogerbek, Aizhan K. Baubekova
pmc-13412150.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Simple SummaryApple orchards around the world are increasingly affected by climate change. Higher temperatures, drought, and changing weather patterns can promote the development of plant-feeding mites, which damage leaves, reduce tree productivity, and decrease fruit quality. Traditional control methods often rely on pesticides, but their repeated use may lead to resistance, harm beneficial organisms, and reduce the ecological stability of orchard ecosystems. This review examines how climate change influences mite outbreaks and discusses sustainable approaches to orchard protection.

pmc-13611481.title: Vision–Radar Semantic Communication for Target-Oriented Visual Sensing: Image Reconstruction and Dynamic State Estimation
pmc-13611481.creator: Hao Xu, Yi Wang, Rikang Zhao, Qiang Liu
pmc-13611481.description: Target-oriented sensing image processing and analysis are important for intelligent surveillance and dynamic sensing applications, where wireless systems need to recover task-relevant visual and state information from heterogeneous sensing data. This study develops a vision–radar semantic communication system for joint target image reconstruction and dynamic state estimation.
